definitions.gloss: round (of golf); a full game of 18 holes
definitions.explanation: A complete game of golf, typically 18 holes. Also used for a half-round (ハーフラウンド, 9 holes).
A single period or stage in boxing, tournaments, discussions, or negotiations.

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}にラウンドする。
examples.english: Play a round of golf on the weekend.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{天気|てんき}がいいから、{気持|きも}ちのいいラウンドになった。
examples.english: The weather was good today, so it was a pleasant round.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めてのラウンドで{緊張|きんちょう}したが、{同伴者|どうはんしゃ}に{助|たす}けられて{楽|たの}しめた。
examples.english: I was nervous on my first round, but my playing partners helped me enjoy it.

examples.japanese: {第|だい}3ラウンド{開始|かいし}。
{交渉|こうしょう}は{次|つぎ}のラウンドに{持|も}ち{越|こ}された。
examples.english: Negotiations were carried over to the next round.

examples.japanese: ボクシングの{試合|しあい}は12ラウンドまで{行|い}ったが、{判定|はんてい}{勝|が}ちとなった。
examples.english: The boxing match went to 12 rounds, and it was decided by judges' decision.

notes:
A loanword from English "round." Most commonly associated with golf in everyday Japanese.

USAGE:
In casual conversation, ラウンド without further context almost always means a round of golf. For boxing and tournaments, the context (ボクシング, {試合|しあい}, etc.) is usually provided. ラウンドする is used as a suru-verb meaning "to play a round of golf." In business contexts, ラウンド can refer to rounds of funding ({資金調達|しきんちょうたつ}ラウンド) or rounds of negotiation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ラウンドする: to play a round of golf
- ラウンドを{回|まわ}る: to go around the course
- {第|だい}1ラウンド: round one, first round
- {最終|さいしゅう}ラウンド: final round
- ハーフラウンド: half round (9 holes of golf)
- {練習|れんしゅう}ラウンド: practice round

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {回戦|かいせん}: round (of a tournament) — the native counter for tournament rounds ({一回戦|いっかいせん} = first round)
- {局|きょく}: round, game — used for go, shogi, and similar board games
- セット: set — used in tennis, volleyball, and similar sports
